overview: Equatorial Guinea is a small country in Central Africa, made up of a mainland region and several islands. Its capital is Malabo, on the island of Bioko, although a new capital is being built on the mainland. It became independent from Spain in 1968 and is the only country in Africa with Spanish as an official language. Oil has been its main export since the 1990s.

geography.text: The mainland, called Río Muni, lies between Cameroon and Gabon and is covered by rainforest. The island of Bioko, in the Gulf of Guinea, is volcanic and mountainous. The country also includes Annobón, a small island far to the south-west.
